TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_order,
         order_id TYPE i,
         amount   TYPE i,
       END OF ty_order.
DATA lt_orders TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_order
  WITH EMPTY KEY.
APPEND VALUE #( order_id = 9 amount = 200 ) TO lt_orders.
APPEND VALUE #( order_id = 7 amount = 100 ) TO lt_orders.
DATA(ls_first) = lt_orders[ 1 ].
DATA lt_processed_ids TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF i WITH EMPTY KEY.
LOOP AT lt_orders INTO DATA(ls_order).
  APPEND ls_order-order_id TO lt_processed_ids.
ENDLOOP.
title: STANDARD: preserve arrival order
intro: Choose this when row order or position is the useful property.
context: Self-contained method-body fragment. Numeric values are local fixtures. lt_processed_ids records the actual processing order.
outcome: ls_first contains order 9. Sequential processing keeps the append order: 9, then 7.
caveat: The primary index is not an order_id index. A free-key search normally scans this table; a suitable secondary key can offer another access path. Index 1 is safe here because two rows were appended.

highlights.label: A sequence, not a unique lookup
highlights.explanation: EMPTY KEY imposes no business-key uniqueness.

highlights.label: Position follows insertion
highlights.explanation: The first row is order 9, even though 7 is numerically smaller.

code:
TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_order,
         customer TYPE i,
         order_id TYPE i,
         amount   TYPE i,
       END OF ty_order.
DATA lt_orders TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_order
  WITH UNIQUE KEY customer order_id.
INSERT VALUE #( customer = 2 order_id = 9 amount = 200 )
  INTO TABLE lt_orders.
INSERT VALUE #( customer = 1 order_id = 7 amount = 100 )
  INTO TABLE lt_orders.
INSERT VALUE #( customer = 2 order_id = 8 amount = 50 )
  INTO TABLE lt_orders.
DATA(total) = 0.
LOOP AT lt_orders INTO DATA(ls_order) WHERE customer = 2.
  total = total + ls_order-amount.
ENDLOOP.
title: SORTED: process one customer’s orders
intro: The leading key groups the rows needed by this lookup.
context: Self-contained method-body fragment. Every (customer, order_id) pair is unique. All amounts are unitless fixture values.
outcome: Customer 2 is processed in order_id order: 8, then 9; total is 250. The complete table key order is (1,7), (2,8), (2,9).
caveat: The optimized selection uses equality on the leading key component customer. Searching by order_id alone is a different access pattern. Handle duplicate-key inserts in real input.

highlights.label: Order belongs to the table type
highlights.explanation: INSERT places each row according to customer and order_id; no separate SORT is needed.

CLASS lcl_order_helper DEFINITION FINAL.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-DATA class_starts TYPE i READ-ONLY.
    CLASS-DATA created TYPE i READ-ONLY.
    DATA order_id TYPE i READ-ONLY.
    CLASS-METHODS class_constructor.
    METHODS constructor IMPORTING order_id TYPE i.
ENDCLASS.
CLASS lcl_order_helper IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD class_constructor.
    class_starts = class_starts + 1.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD constructor.
    me->order_id = order_id.
    created = created + 1.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
"Caller, for example inside a separate main method:
DATA(first) = NEW lcl_order_helper( order_id = 7 ).
DATA(second) = NEW lcl_order_helper( order_id = 9 ).
ASSERT lcl_order_helper=>class_starts = 1.
ASSERT lcl_order_helper=>created = 2.
ASSERT first->order_id = 7.
ASSERT second->order_id = 9.
title: One class initialization, two object initializations
intro: The counters make the different lifetimes visible.
context: Local class definition and implementation, followed by a separate caller fragment. Run the caller once in a fresh internal session. Counters and ASSERT statements are teaching instrumentation, not a recommended application design.
outcome: Both objects keep their own order ID. The class initialization counter is 1 and the object counter is 2.
caveat: Earlier object creation in the same internal session changes created. A static method or attribute access may initialize the class before NEW. This example has no inheritance; do not infer superclass constructor rules from it.

highlights.label: Once for the class
highlights.explanation: The runtime calls class_constructor once in this internal session.

highlights.label: Once for each new object
highlights.explanation: me->order_id belongs to this object; created belongs to the class.

highlights.label: Observe the result
highlights.explanation: Two successful NEW calls run two instance constructors.

code:
CLASS zcl_study_sum DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES if_amdp_marker_hdb.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_item,
             quantity TYPE i,
           END OF ty_item,
           ty_items TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_item WITH EMPTY KEY.
    CLASS-METHODS sum_quantities
      IMPORTING VALUE(lt_items) TYPE ty_items
      EXPORTING VALUE(total) TYPE i.
ENDCLASS.
CLASS zcl_study_sum IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD sum_quantities BY DATABASE PROCEDURE
    FOR HDB LANGUAGE SQLSCRIPT OPTIONS READ-ONLY.
    SELECT COALESCE(SUM(quantity), 0) INTO total FROM :lt_items;
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
"Separate ABAP caller fragment:
DATA lt_items TYPE zcl_study_sum=>ty_items.
lt_items = VALUE #( ( quantity = 40 ) ( quantity = 60 ) ).
zcl_study_sum=>sum_quantities(
  EXPORTING lt_items = lt_items
  IMPORTING total = DATA(total) ).
title: AMDP procedure: call a method
intro: Input and output parameters carry data across the ABAP/HANA boundary.
context: Global AMDP class for Standard ABAP on HANA. Create zcl_study_sum and place the separate caller inside an ABAP method. This is not a local class. No database table is required.
outcome: The expected total is 100; empty input produces 0. The procedure has EXPORTING total, not RETURNING.
caveat: This sum is intentionally trivial and does not justify AMDP. Use ordinary ABAP or SQL for it. Integer overflow, exceptions and real authorization need handling in a real calculation. Check the target release’s additional client-safety declarations before using this in ABAP Cloud.

highlights.label: Declare the procedure contract
highlights.explanation: The marker identifies an AMDP class. Both parameters are passed by VALUE.

highlights.label: Execute SQLScript on HANA
highlights.explanation: COALESCE converts the empty aggregate’s NULL to zero.

highlights.label: Call from ABAP
highlights.explanation: The caller receives the output through IMPORTING.

title: CDS table function: declare the query shape
intro: CDS defines the parameter and result columns; an AMDP method provides the rows.
context: Separate CDS data definition ZTF_Study_Amounts for a Standard ABAP/HANA sandbox with CDS table-function support. Its associated global class is shown in the next example. The deliberately client-independent fixture contains no real business data.
outcome: Consumers see p_minimum and exactly two result columns. The implementation must return compatible types and columns in this declared order.
caveat: This classic annotation is shown for the stated Standard ABAP context. Check current client-safety annotations for ABAP Cloud. Do not copy client independence to real client-dependent business data, and do not treat this definition as an authorization check.

highlights.label: A query contract
highlights.explanation: The result is a table of order IDs and amounts, filtered by an input threshold.

highlights.label: Connect the implementation
highlights.explanation: This method will be declared FOR TABLE FUNCTION, without manually repeating its parameter list.

code:
CLASS zcl_study_amounts DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES if_amdp_marker_hdb.
    CLASS-METHODS read_amounts FOR TABLE FUNCTION ztf_study_amounts.
ENDCLASS.
CLASS zcl_study_amounts IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD read_amounts BY DATABASE FUNCTION
    FOR HDB LANGUAGE SQLSCRIPT OPTIONS READ-ONLY
    USING zt_study_amount.
    RETURN SELECT order_id, amount FROM zt_study_amount
      WHERE amount >= :p_minimum;
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
"Separate ABAP consumer fragment:
SELECT FROM ztf_study_amounts( p_minimum = 50 )
  FIELDS order_id, amount
  ORDER BY order_id
  INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_amounts).
title: Read a CDS entity, not its implementation method
intro: FOR TABLE FUNCTION obtains the method contract from the CDS definition.
context: Standard ABAP/HANA: requires the preceding CDS table function and own table zt_study_amount. The global class and ABAP caller belong in separate places. The client-independent fixture has unique order_id INT4, amount INT4 and no client column; rows are (7,40), (9,60), (11,10). These are own teaching objects, not SAP APIs.
outcome: SELECT returns one row: order_id 9, amount 60. No direct ABAP call to read_amounts is made.
caveat: The simple filter could be written directly in ABAP SQL; it only demonstrates the contract. Real business sources require client safety, authorization, released dependencies and numeric-type checks. READ-ONLY prevents writes; it does not supply those controls.

highlights.label: Implement a database function
highlights.explanation: The function is read-only and declares its database dependency.

highlights.label: Return matching rows
highlights.explanation: The parameter p_minimum comes from the CDS contract.

highlights.label: Consume through SELECT
highlights.explanation: The CDS entity can be a query source. ORDER BY belongs in the consuming query when order matters.
